title: ATP AI/ML recategorization: why a URL can start blocking with no policy change
aliases: url was fine last week now blocked

ai-ml-detection.statement: ATP's AI/ML tools detect C2 botnets, credential theft and phishing URLs by analyzing URLs that are uncategorized or in the Miscellaneous or Unknown category, and categorize them under Botnet Protection or Fraud Protection (Phishing) advanced threats, or leave them in Miscellaneous or Unknown.

quotes: The AI/ML tools detect C2 botnets, credential theft, and phishing URLs by analyzing the URLs that are not categorized and those in the Miscellaneous or Unknown category.
The tools then categorize the URLs under Botnet Protection or Fraud Protection (Phishing) advanced threats or the Miscellaneous or Unknown URL category.

blocking-can-change-without-edit.statement: A URL that was uncategorized or Miscellaneous or Unknown, and so not blocked, can start to be blocked after the AI/ML tools move it into a Botnet or Phishing category whose toggle is set to Block, with no admin edit to any policy.
blocking-can-change-without-edit.conditions: A consequence of the categorization moving a URL into a blocked group. No source shows a specific case, or how quickly a recategorization takes effect.

dashboard-shows-event.title: Where an AI/ML recategorization shows up
dashboard-shows-event.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Security Dashboard shows the reclassification event.' No captured page says a recategorization is logged as an event. What would resolve it: a log or Security Dashboard export from a URL known to have been recategorized.

separate-toggle.title: Whether AI/ML recategorization has its own on and off control
separate-toggle.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'When enabled, ATP's AI/ML tools analyze uncategorized or Miscellaneous-or-Unknown URLs.' The help page describes the AI/ML tools without any toggle, and the ATP settings object has no key for one. What would resolve it: the console view of a tenant, or a support answer.
